name: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

controls.title: Information Flow Enforcement
controls.description: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on approved authorizations and security policies.
controls.guidance: Information flow enforcement regulates where information is allowed to travel within a system and between systems. Firewalls, boundary protection devices, and routers with access control lists (ACLs) must restrict traffic so that default permit-any policies are strictly prohibited.

controls.title: Boundary Protection
controls.description: Monitor and control communications at external boundaries of the system and at key internal boundaries within the system; connect to external networks only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with enterprise security architecture.
controls.guidance: Managed interfaces include routers, firewalls, and proxy gateways. Firewalls must separate public, demilitarized (DMZ), and private enterprise zones. Deny by default must be configured on all ingress/egress points.

controls.title: Access Enforcement
controls.description: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
controls.guidance: Network devices must restrict management access (SSH/HTTPS) to dedicated bastion hosts and administrative subnets.

controls.title: Event Logging
controls.description: Identify that the system is capable of logging the specified event types: password changes, failed logins, administrative privilege escalations, firewall rule drops.
controls.guidance: Network security appliances must forward syslog messages to a central SIEM/PostgreSQL repository in real time.

controls.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
controls.description: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users (or processes acting on behalf of organizational users).
controls.guidance: Enforce AAA authentication and disable shared administrative accounts on network devices.

controls.title: Least Functionality
controls.description: Configure the system to provide only essential capabilities and prohibit or restrict the use of non-essential services, protocols, and ports.
controls.guidance: Disable insecure legacy protocols such as Telnet, HTTP, and SNMPv1/v2c across all network interfaces.
